title: Weak object pronouns and their position
goal: Use με, σε, τον, του, μου… in the right case and the right place.

blocks.text: Everyday Greek replaces objects with short unstressed pronouns that cling to the verb. The **accusative** set is the direct object (Τον ξέρω 'I know him'); the **genitive** set is the indirect object (Του μιλάω 'I talk to him') and also the possessive after a noun (ο φίλος του). Getting the case right is half the work; position is the other half.

blocks.title: Phone calls: σε παίρνω, σου τηλεφωνώ
blocks.text: Greek has two everyday ways to say 'call someone', and they take different cases. **Τηλεφωνώ** takes the genitive: **Σου τηλεφώνησα** 'I called you'. The more colloquial **παίρνω τηλέφωνο** takes the accusative: **Σε πήρα τηλέφωνο**, or just **Θα σε πάρω** 'I'll call you'. People answer with **Ναι;**, **Παρακαλώ** or **Λέγετε**, and friends often with **Έλα**. A deliberate **αναπάντητη** 'missed call' is a free signal: **Κάνε μου μια αναπάντητη όταν φτάσεις** 'Give me a missed call when you get there'. The call ends with **Τα λέμε!** 'Talk soon!'

**Verbs that take the genitive where English has a direct object:** τηλεφωνώ (Του τηλεφώνησα 'I phoned him'), αρέσει (Μου αρέσει 'I like it', literally 'it pleases to me'), λείπει (Μου λείπεις 'I miss you'). Learn these as chunks.

blocks.title: Το δώρο της Κατερίνας
blocks.text:
— Νίκο, ξέρεις ότι η Κατερίνα έχει γενέθλια το Σάββατο;

— Ναι, μου το είπε ο Γιώργος χθες. Της πήρες δώρο;

— Όχι ακόμα. Σκέφτηκα ένα βιβλίο, αλλά δεν ξέρω αν της αρέσει το διάβασμα.

— Της αρέσει πολύ! Την είδα στο μετρό με ένα βιβλίο στο χέρι την περασμένη εβδομάδα.

— Ωραία. Ποιο βιβλίο όμως; Εσύ την ξέρεις καλύτερα.

— Μου είπε κάποτε ότι θέλει να διαβάσει Καζαντζάκη. Πάρε της τον «Ζορμπά». Θα τον λατρέψει.

— Καλή ιδέα! Θα τον αγοράσω αύριο. Μπορείς να τον τυλίξεις εσύ; Εγώ δεν ξέρω να τυλίγω δώρα.

— Εντάξει, φέρ' τον μου την Παρασκευή. Και μην της πεις τίποτα, θέλουμε να είναι έκπληξη!

— Δεν θα της πω λέξη. Αλλά ο Γιώργος; Αυτός τα λέει όλα!

— Θα του τηλεφωνήσω απόψε και θα του το εξηγήσω.
blocks.en:
— Nikos, do you know it's Katerina's birthday on Saturday?

— Yes, Giorgos told me yesterday. Have you got her a present?

— Not yet. I thought of a book, but I don't know if she likes reading.

— She loves it! I saw her on the metro with a book in her hand last week.

— Great. But which book? You know her better.

— She once told me she wants to read Kazantzakis. Get her 'Zorba'. She'll adore it.

— Good idea! I'll buy it tomorrow. Can you wrap it? I don't know how to wrap presents.

— Fine, bring it to me on Friday. And don't tell her anything, we want it to be a surprise!

— I won't say a word to her. But what about Giorgos? He tells everyone everything!

— I'll phone him tonight and explain it to him.

gloss.τυλίξεις: τυλίγω — to wrap (perfective, 2sg: να τον τυλίξεις 'that you wrap it')
gloss.φέρ: φέρνω — bring (imperative φέρε, shortened before a pronoun: φέρ' τον μου 'bring it to me')
gloss.λατρέψει: λατρεύω — to adore (perfective, 3sg: θα τον λατρέψει 'she'll love it')
gloss.Σκέφτηκα: σκέφτομαι — to think (simple past: I thought of)

questions.prompt: Γιατί θα τηλεφωνήσει ο Νίκος στον Γιώργο;
questions.answer: Για να μην πει τίποτα στην Κατερίνα

items.why: Direct object, feminine: τη(ν).
τηλεφωνώ takes the genitive.

items.prompt: I like the music: ___ αρέσει η μουσική.
items.why: αρέσει: the person who likes is genitive.
Literally 'you are missing to me'.
With an imperative the pronouns follow the verb.
Before the verb, genitive first, then accusative.
With μη(ν) + subjunctive the pronouns stay before the verb.
Nothing between pronoun and verb, and δεν θα comes first.
The possessive follows the noun.
It may follow an adjective: Holton §4.1.
Imperative + pronoun, and a second accent appears on the verb.

items.prompt: Do you know them (f.)? Yes, I know them.
items.why: Before the verb only τις is possible.

items.prompt: I'm writing to my mother: ___ γράφω της μητέρας μου.
items.why: Indirect object doubled by a genitive pronoun; in speech σε + acc. is more common (Γράφω στη μητέρα μου).
After a comparative the genitive pronoun gives the second term.

items.prompt: Replace the object with a pronoun: Βλέπω **τη Μαρία**.
items.why: A direct object becomes accusative τη(ν) and goes before the verb.

items.prompt: Replace with a pronoun: Μιλάω **στον Πέτρο**.
items.why: σε + noun (indirect object) becomes the genitive pronoun του.

items.prompt: Replace both objects: Δίνω **το κλειδί** **στη μητέρα μου**.
items.why: Two pronouns before the verb: genitive (της) first, then accusative (το).

items.prompt: Replace both objects: Θα στείλω **τα γράμματα** **στους φίλους μου**.
items.why: θα + genitive + accusative + verb: nothing else may come between θα and the verb.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *Call me!* (sg., παίρνω τηλέφωνο)
items.why: After an imperative the pronoun follows; παίρνω τηλέφωνο takes the accusative (με).
τηλεφωνώ takes the genitive: της, not τη.

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *Do you like it?* (sg., αρέσει)
items.why: The person who likes is genitive (σου); the thing liked is the subject.
With λείπω the people missed are the subject (λείπουν) and the person missing them is genitive (μας).

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *Don't wait for me!* (sg.)
items.why: With μη(ν) the pronoun stays before the verb; περιμένω takes a direct object (με).

items.prompt: Say in Greek: *Tell it to them!* (sg., λέω)
items.why: After the imperative both pronouns follow the verb: genitive τους + accusative το (or το τους).
Direct object of βλέπω: 2sg accusative σε.
βοηθώ takes a direct object, so accusative τον (English 'help' has no 'to' either).
In standard Greek ρωτάω takes the person in the accusative: Τη ρώτησα.
θα, then genitive, then accusative, then the verb.
The pronoun follows the imperative; a second accent appears when the stress is on the third syllable from the end.
The 3rd plural genitive is τους for all genders; τις and τα are accusative.

items.prompt: Ποιος σου το είπε; — ___ είπε η Μαρία.
items.why: Indirect object genitive μου first, then direct object το.
